title: An Empirical Preregistered Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for Intent-to-Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We preregistered and ran a paired confirmatory experiment (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) that compares LLM-only configuration generation to a guarded generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline for intent-to-configuration NetOps tasks. Under a frozen plan we executed 200 stratified paired trials in a Dockerized Mininet emulator with a deterministic validator and gpt-5-mini. Observed confirmatory outcomes: baseline verifier-accepted = 200/200; GVR verifier-accepted = 200/200; paired contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference = 0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed=1729), exact paired-test p = 1.0. The preregistered shared-generation semantics (one LLM candidate per task evaluated under both arms) and the constrained emulation/validator/model scope explain the null paired difference; this null therefore maps to those explicit boundary conditions rather than implying a general absence of GVR benefit. We publish all preregistration, raw responses, validator traces, provider-call traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts (see execution_manifest and hashes) to enable reproducible reanalysis and follow-up experiments that relax the shared-generation constraint, expand validator coverage, or vary model sampling.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) can translate operator intent into device configuration, offering automation potential for network operations (NetOps). However, unguarded LLM outputs risk introducing reachability loss, policy violations, or availability regressions. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipelines combine generation with deterministic validation and bounded repair loops to reduce such operational risk. Prior NetOps benchmarks and pipelines (e.g., NetConfEval, OpsEval, NetEval) explore components of this stack but rarely publish preregistered, artifact-backed, paired comparisons that fix design choices and reproducibly record all execution traces. We preregistered (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) a within-task paired evaluation to measure whether a guarded GVR pipeline reduces operational-failure rates (reachability loss or policy violation) relative to LLM-only generation under a well-defined emulator and deterministic validator. The contributions are (1) a fully preregistered paired confirmatory run (n=200 pairs) with frozen analysis plan and published artifacts; (2) deterministic reconciliation and full per-episode hashing; (3) an artifact-grounded report of the observed null paired difference and explicit accounting of the boundary conditions that produced it.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and benchmarks investigate LLMs for NetOps and AIOps and propose verifier-assisted generation strategies (Wang et al., NetConfEval 2024; Liu et al., OpsEval 2023; Miao et al., NetEval 2023). Work on verifier-assisted pipelines and self-repair in software engineering highlights benefits of generate–validate–repair patterns, but prior evaluations often lack preregistration, deterministic artifact publication, or paired within-task designs that avoid sampling confounds. Our study adopts the GVR architecture but emphasizes preregistration, deterministic auditing, and an explicit boundary-conditioned interpretation of results.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. We preregistered GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1 and froze: research question, estimands, stratified sampling (200 confirmatory tasks), validator rules, contamination thresholds (≥80% token overlap exclusion rule), retry policy, analysis plan (paired bootstrap 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), and stopping rules. The preregistration and full JSON are archived in the evidence bundle and execution_manifest. Key preregistered design choice (explicit and archived). generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false): for each task a single LLM-produced candidate was generated and that identical candidate was evaluated under both arms (baseline and guarded). This choice (preregistered and implemented) produced one model call per task and is recorded in execution/model_configuration.json and execution_manifest.json. Execution harness. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model declared: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Emulation and validation. We used a Dockerized Mininet emulator and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) that parses normalized configs, enforces workflow and safety constraints (e.g., "must be down for MTU/VLAN change"), runs reachability/policy probes, and returns verifier-accept/reject. Task bank and sampling. Confirmatory bank = 200 tasks stratified over five protocol/focus clusters × two interaction modalities (≈20 tasks per cluster). Contamination checks. Automated token-overlap checks per the preregistered rule flagged no confirmatory tasks (analysis/contamination_summary.csv). Analysis and inference (preregistered). Primary estimand: paired difference in the binary operational-failure indicator (1 if failure observed; 0 otherwise). Primary inference: paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, fixed seed = 1729) and preregistered paired test (Wilcoxon signed-rank). For the observed degenerate 2×2 contingency we report the exact paired contingency assessment (McNemar two-sided) and present the archived counts and p-value (analysis artifacts). Reproducibility. All artifacts (task manifest, LLM outputs, provider-call traces, scoring JSONs, validator traces, analysis scripts, execution_manifest with SHA-256 hashes) are published; representative artifact paths and hashes are cited below so readers may deterministically reproduce arithmetic and checks.
sections.results: Execution and primary outcomes. Execution completed as preregistered: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, model_calls_used = 200 (shared-initial semantics produced one model call per confirmatory task), failed_episode_count = 0 (execution_manifest.json). Confirmatory scoring (archived): baseline verifier-accepted configurations = 200/200; guarded verifier-accepted configurations = 200/200. Paired contingency (archived analysis): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA-256 7bc1bd2a...). Paired estimate and inference: paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl); exact paired contingency test p = 1.0 (McNemar two-sided; archived). Repair activity (preregistered exploratory). No repair was applied for any confirmatory episode: repair_attempts = 0 across all 200 confirmatory tasks (scoring JSON fields validator_trace.repair_applied == false; representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json, SHA-256 9235bce7875c1717dff5ac6be49c5769929b4e85...). Deterministic reconciliation. All bookkeeping and call-accounting checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Representative artifacts. Example confirmatory artifacts (paths and hashes): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA-256 f8de4d6e1a625e42...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA-256 9235bce7...), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256 a40e96e2...). The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and boundary conditions. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one LLM candidate per task evaluated under both arms) was implemented as planned and explains the observed null paired difference: no repairs were invoked (repair_attempts = 0), so baseline and guarded outputs were identical for every confirmatory task. Thus the confirmatory null is an artifact of explicitly preregistered design choices and the constrained testbed (emulator + deterministic validator + single model). It does not imply that GVR lacks value in broader settings. Scenarios where GVR is expected to show measurable benefit include (i) independent-condition-generation (produce separate LLM candidates per arm), (ii) stochastic model sampling or alternative model families, (iii) richer device/firmware semantics or production heterogeneity not captured by the emulator, (iv) weaker or incomplete validator rule coverage, or (v) adversarial/novel fault modes. Practical recommendations and reproducible follow-ups. To measure incremental repair value one should preregister independent-condition-generation (separate LLM calls per arm), ensure baseline nonzero failure rates in pilots, expand validator coverage, or evaluate multiple models and stochastic seeds. All artifacts to support such follow-ups are published in the execution bundle (execution_manifest lists files and SHA-256 hashes). Threats to validity. Internal validity is preserved by preregistration and deterministic reconciliation, but the shared-generation design constrained the capacity to observe repair-driven differences. Construct validity is limited by the finite rule set of the deterministic validator and emulator realism. External validity is limited by single-model testing and synthetic task bank; generalization to production device families is not claimed. Conclusion. Under the preregistered shared-generation semantics and the controlled emulator+validator scope, both baseline and guarded GVR produced verifier-acceptable configurations on all confirmatory tasks (200/200 each). The null paired difference maps to these boundary conditions. We make all artifacts available to enable reproducible reanalysis and planned follow-up runs that relax the shared-generation constraint or increase model/validator diversity.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation comparing LLM-only generation and a guarded GVR pipeline on 200 stratified intent-to-configuration tasks with gpt-5-mini. Both conditions produced verifier-accepted configurations for every confirmatory task (200/200), giving a paired difference of 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]) and exact-test p = 1.0. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics—one LLM candidate per task evaluated under both arms—and the constrained emulation and deterministic validator explain this null: repairs were not invoked for the confirmatory bank. The result therefore documents a concrete boundary condition where GVR did not change verifier acceptance, rather than proving GVR is unnecessary generally. All preregistration, raw outputs, validator/provider traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts (with SHA-256 hashes) are published in the execution bundle to permit reproducible reanalysis and follow-up experiments that relax the shared-generation choice or broaden model/validator diversity.

Key preregistered design choices (archived and executed): generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (a single LLM candidate per task was produced and that identical candidate was evaluated under both baseline and guarded arms); task bank stratification (200 confirmatory tasks across five protocol-focus clusters × two modalities); maximum_model_calls = 400; planned_episode_count = 400. All raw artifacts—task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256 c1bd4a09...), per-episode responses (execution/responses/* with per-file SHA-256 listed in execution_manifest), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*), validator/traces and scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), the execution manifest, and analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl)—are published with SHA-256 hashes in the supplied evidence bundle so third parties can reproduce the deterministic arithmetic and bookkeeping. Preregistered contamination criteria were applied (≥80% token overlap exclusion); no confirmatory tasks were flagged. Repairs and iterations: preregistered repair policy permitted bounded repairs; observed repair_applied = false for every confirmatory episode (repair_attempts = 0; see execution/scoring JSONs). Deterministic reconciliation: all accounting checks (pair counts, model-call reconciliation, cache metrics) passed and are archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Deviations: none that alter core facts; the shared_initial_candidate design choice was preregistered and executed as specified. Limitations and scope: the experiment tests explicit boundary conditions (single-model gpt-5-mini, shared-initial generation semantics, Dockerized Mininet emulation, deterministic validator). The reported null paired difference therefore pertains to those boundary conditions; it does not prove the absence of GVR value under independent-generation, stochastic-sampling, multi-model, or production-device settings. The immutable master prompt reference above (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 1872df1e...) documents the exact initial master prompt as required by the track.
limitations: Emulation and synthetic-task scope: confirmatory bank used synthetic vendor-like templates in a Dockerized Mininet emulator; production firmware/device diversity is not represented.
Single-model scope: only gpt-5-mini was evaluated in the confirmatory run; results do not generalize across model families or sampling regimes.

Shared-generation preregistration choice: generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one LLM candidate per task evaluated by both arms) was preregistered and executed; because no repairs were invoked (repair_attempts = 0) baseline and guarded outputs were identical, mechanically preventing observation of repair-driven differences in this run.

Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite rule set and probes; gaps in validator rules or emulator realism would limit construct validity relative to real production environments.

Power-plan assumption violated: the preregistered power calculation assumed nonzero baseline failure rates; observed baseline success = 100% invalidated that assumption and reduces the confirmatory test’s informativeness outside the preregistered boundary conditions.
Contamination-detection limits: automated token-overlap checks flagged 0 confirmatory tasks, but undiscoverable overlap between model pretraining data and task templates cannot be fully excluded.
